acceptance_results.evidence: git status and git diff in the seeded run directory show no change after the run; the memo itself asserts a clean work tree.

All three named risks handled concretely and beyond the sol-high run's depth: token invalidation via security_epoch/jti/session checks, a signed PrincipalEnvelope replacing stored bearer tokens, minimum_security_revision demands, and the grant-versus-revoke consistency asymmetry; cross-service drift bounded by digest-pinned shadow comparison with a five-way mismatch taxonomy, stable-cohort canaries, and an explicit ban on automatic local fallback because stale local policy can resurrect revoked access; audit continuity via a shared schema introduced before cutover, producer=legacy tagging with a cutover marker, and joining decision events against caller enforcement events to detect four distinct integrity failures.

Cutover happens per stable cohort behind control-plane settings; rollback reverts a whole cohort within a validated compatibility window while local runs as reverse shadow, and automatic per-failure fallback is forbidden precisely because it would apply stale allows — keeping decisions consistent under rollback. Final local-adapter removal is gated on rollback and outage drills passing; earlier stages are additive no-ops.
